plain_definition: An arrangement giving a listing exchange access to trading data from the market where an exchange-traded product's underlying asset, or a derivative on it, actually trades, so the exchange can help detect fraud and manipulation. An exchange typically satisfies this by showing that market is a member of the Intermarket Surveillance Group (ISG), a group of exchanges and regulators that share surveillance information with one another, or by entering into a bespoke surveillance-sharing agreement with that market directly.
formal_definition: Cited in SEC orders and notices reviewing proposed rule changes under Exchange Act Section 19(b) as one basis for finding that a national securities exchange's rules are designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, as Section 6(b)(5) (15 U.S.C. 78f(b)(5)) requires; also incorporated as an eligibility pathway in the SEC's generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares (Release No. 34-103995, 17 September 2025).
